articles.title: ‘Family Stone 2’ Gets Official Title ‘The Families Stone’ and Sets Cast: Rachel McAdams, Sarah Jessica Parker and More Returning
articles.summary: Searchlight has officially announced “The Family Stone 2,” a sequel to the 2005 holiday classic from returning writer and director Tom Bezucha. The follow-up is officially titled “The Families Stones” and will feature the returns of many of the original’s main cast members, including Rachel McAdams…
body: The project was first revealed in November 2025 by Bezucha. The announcement came shortly after the death of Diane Keaton, who played the Stone family matriarch Sybil in the first movie.

“I’ve been haunted by the loss of Sybil for months now while I worked on it, and so this was a blow on a tender bruise already,” Bezucha said at the time. “Mentally, I’ve been spending time in that house where I’ve been missing her for a while already.”

“The Family Stone” follows Sarah Jessica Parker as businesswoman Meredith Morton, who goes home for Christmas with her boyfriend Everett, played by Dermot Mulroney, to win over his eccentric extended family during their annual holiday celebration. The title “Family Stone” has a double meaning. Stone is Everett’s family name. “Family Stone” is also a reference to Sybil’s mother’s wedding ring, which Meredith hopes to prove she is worthy of during her visit.
Released in Dec. of 2005, “The Family Stone” opened strong to $12 million against its budget of just $18 million. It went on to earn $92 million worldwide during its box office run.

body: The project grew out of Nishikawa’s research for “Under the Open Sky,” her 2021 drama starring Yakusho Koji as a man modeled on a real war orphan who drifted into crime and prison after growing up on the streets of postwar Japan. Yakusho returns for “Children Untold” as Jinpei. That earlier project left Nishikawa wanting to tell the broader story of the children who survived Japan’s defeat, and of the underworld that absorbed many of them.

Nishikawa began developing “Children Untold” in 2020, during pandemic lockdowns that had shut down theaters and cut off her usual route to an audience. Digging into archival testimony, she found a history that had gone largely unexamined. “The children who were orphaned were, of course, still children at the time. They had no means of making their voices heard or appealing for help,” Nishikawa says.

articles.title: Girl Group review – Rebel Wilson’s dreadful music comedy is a spice-free wannabe
articles.summary: Toronto film festival: the actor turned writer-director’s ode to girl groups is a shoddily made and embarrassingly unfunny catastrophe. There were plentiful on-paper delights for certain music fans of a certain generation promised at Toronto’s splashy Friday-night premiere of pop comedy Girl Group.
body: Wilson’s aggrieved ex-star gets into a car crash after drinking in a laughably unconvincing idea of LA (the entire film was gauzily shot in the UK although it could be inside Sora for all I could tell) and is sentenced to community service, which lands her at a youth centre, which then leads her to a wannabe girl group, which then coincides with her finding out about some big competition and whatever.

articles.title: Extended reality takes visitors from the ruins of West Bank to 17th-century Amsterdam at Venice Immersive
articles.summary: From frivolous to serious, virtual nosy passersby to the impact of climate change, the groundbreaking festival draws to a close – but this year the exhibits live on. The first installation one encounters on visiting Venice Immersive, the film festival’s reliably head-spinning showcase for new…
body: The passerby is not real – or rather, he’s only real in the box. He wears a blue suit and speaks with a heavy French accent and tells a tale that would sit badly in polite company. He says that I must have too much time on my hands, to stand hunched over this eyepiece for several minutes on end. “Why do people keep looking inside this box?” he demands. “What is it that they hope to see? It is not reality.”

The name of Celine Daemen’s fabulous installation – Nothing to See Here – is immediately belied by the presence of 67 further exhibits (the organisers refer to them as “experiences”) arranged cheek by jowl on a small dedicated island. But the creepy Frenchman’s contention should not be so lightly brushed aside. Venice Immersive’s projects run the gamut from the frivolous to the serious, the escapist to the harrowing. But is the island a backwater or a new-found land? Does it represent reality or different versions of a dream?

articles.title: Luke Evans: ‘As I child I was in love with Harrison Ford as Indiana Jones’
articles.summary: The Hobbit and Fast & Furious actor on the joy of strawberry laces, hating that he’s so hard on himself, and his sneaky way of leaving a meeting. Born in south Wales, Luke Evans, 47, left school at 16 and trained at London Studio Centre before appearing in various West End shows.
body: What is the trait you most deplore in yourself? Being hard on myself, saying negative things in my head that are not helpful.
Aside from a property, what’s the most expensive thing you’ve bought? My business. BDXY is a clothing brand I started with my partner three years ago with no investment.

If you could bring something extinct back to life, what would you choose? My great-aunt Lala, who I named my dog after. Lala was 94 when she died and I was seven. We saw her every Saturday and I’ve got tape recordings of me and her singing. I was the apple of her eye and she would have been thrilled being part of my journey.
Who is your celebrity crush? As a child, Harrison Ford in Indiana Jones. I was in love with him.

articles.title: ‘Smudge the Blades’ Isn’t Your ‘Heated Rivalry’-Style Canadian Hockey Drama
articles.summary: Cody Lightning’s feature film is all business on the ice — an underdog dramedy about a struggling Indigenous team fighting racism outside the rink.
body: Unlike the hit Canadian TV drama and its off-ice romance, Cody Lightning’s underdog Indigenous hockey team dramedy is mostly high-energy on-ice play. And no actors needed training in how to skate before cameras on the indie rolled.

Of course, Smudge the Blades — Lightning’s second feature headed to the Toronto Film Festival for a world premiere (the first being TK) — does mirror, in parts, Disney’s 1992 hockey comedy The Mighty Ducks. But Coach Willie in the Canadian indie is no win-at-all-costs lawyer-turned-coach, as was Emilio Estevez as Gordon Bombay.

The high-strung coach in Smudge the Blades is first played by Ed Helms, until the Blades are kicked out of the league. This being an Indigenous hockey team film, it’s left to Lightning as the local arena Zamboni driver to take over coaching the losing Blades team.
Significantly, Coach Willie has no Estevez-style motivational speeches to get do-nothings to push past their limits to championship glory.
points: Cody Lightning’s feature film is all business on the ice — an underdog dramedy about a struggling Indigenous team fighting racism outside the rink.

articles.title: ‘Club Kid’, ‘Wicker’ Producer on Cannes Sales and When Ikea Gets In on Your Trailer Launch: “Sometimes the Internet Just Does Its Job”
articles.summary: With both 'Club Kid‘ and ‘The Debut‘ set to screen at TIFF, Ryan Heller talks Topic Studios’ big year, including 'Wicker’s unexpected Internet virality.
body: It’s a dream for every producer that the theatrical trailer for their independently made, artist-driven feature goes viral (in a good way) online. It’s a whole other level when a big-box store gets in on the fun.

“It shows the power of an exciting hook in a marketplace where it is hard to get people’s attention, and it’s hard to rely on casual moviegoing to lift your movie. It has become about creating theatrical urgency,” says Heller of the unexpected but welcome attention.

Even before the online notoriety, 2026 was already a banner year for Topic, which sold Jordan Firstman’s debut feature Club Kid to A24 out of the Cannes Film Festival and on Sept. 5 premiered Jesse Eisenberg’s The Debut to rave reviews and plenty of Oscar buzz.
Ahead of TIFF, where both Club Kid and The Debut are screening, Heller talked to THR about Topic’s big year.

articles.title: Grammy-winning US rapper Lil Durk acquitted in murder-for-hire trial
articles.summary: The Chicago rapper was arrested in 2024 and accused of involvement in a shooting that killed the cousin of rival rapper Quando Rondo.
body: Grammy-winning rapper Lil Durk was acquitted on Friday of all charges in a federal murder-for-hire case accusing him of orchestrating the revenge killing of a man shot dead in a daytime ambush in Los Angeles four years ago.
Defence lawyer Drew Findling said the recording artist, whose real name is Durk Devontay Banks, was "thankful" following the verdict.
Lil Durk has had seven albums in the US Billboard chart's top five since 2019 and has also collaborated with stars including Drake and J Cole on hit singles.
Supporters cheered outside a Los Angeles courthouse after the verdict, which came following three days of jury deliberations.

articles.title: Toronto: ‘Purgatory’ Director Navigates Warring Parents and Girl Power in Dark Divorce Comedy
articles.summary: Lindsey Lanzillotta's coming-of-age dramedy and debut feature stars J.K. Simmons, Ruby McGurrin, Abby Elliot and John Reynolds and is set for a world premiere at TIFF.
body: What’s a girl to do when your parents split up and leave your sheltered, suburban home and school life in ruins?

That’s the premise for 1980s-set Purgatory, Lindsay Lanzillotta’s debut feature that stars J.K. Simmons, The Bear ’s Abby Elliot, John Reynolds and Ruby McGurrin in her first movie role as Beatrice Gravel.

Lanzillotta directed Purgatory from a screenplay by Christine Speer and looked to get into Beatrice’s head as, while naive as a coming-of-age tween, she’s also hyper-aware and traumatized by her disrupted home and school life. “It’s like when feelings are on top of your skin, everyone does feel a little fake around you and doesn’t feel what you’re feeling and you wonder, ‘Does anyone see how I’m feeling,’” the director explains.

But in a small town where empathy has virtually disappeared to be replaced by heartlessness and even savagery among Beatrice’s high school friends and their parents, the exception and vital opening for tenderness in Purgatory comes with J.K. Simmons as Father Malone.
